During the year, we invested approximately ₹240 crores in capital expenditure, including our investment in the Sumitomo joint venture, while planning a further ₹200 crores of investment in FY 2026-27.

In FY 2025-26, we invested approximately ` 240 crores in capital expenditure, including our infusion into the Sumitomo joint venture; in the year ahead, we plan to invest a further ` 200 crores, including the remaining preform-related capex.
Growth & demand: The continued rollout of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) is sustaining strong demand for LT/ HT power cables, our own power cable business delivered close to 21% volume growth this year, reflecting exactly this tailwind.

Key Strengths • A diversified revenue base spanning Electrical Cables, Communication Cables and consumer electrical products, with Electrical Cables the primary growth engine, contributing close to 87% of FY26 revenue. • Broad based volume growth across product categories through the year.

Metal based product volumes were lower year on year, but this was largely offset by strong Optic Fibre Cable momentum, with volumes up 34% in the third quarter, underscoring rising data infrastructure demand.
Margins & costs: BACKWARD INTEGRATION We manufacture compounds, copper rods, glass fibres and other raw materials in-house, giving us tighter control over material availability, pricing and quality, and the ability to produce high-quality, cost-effective products consistently.
In addition, we consciously increased inventory by approximately ₹300 crores to secure raw material availability and ensure uninterrupted production during the subsequent months.

Capex & expansion: Given the demand we are already seeing from data centre and AI-led applications, we are now moving with urgency to commission Phase 2 of this expansion, an investment of approximately ₹100 crores that will take our preform capacity to nearly 8 million kilometres of fibre.

Capital Expenditure and Capacity Expansion The Company had committed a capital expenditure of ₹500 Crores over an 18-month period to significantly enhance its manufacturing capacities at Urse (Maharashtra) and Goa facilities.
STRATEGIC INITIATIVES AND CAPACITY EXPANSION Balance Sheet Strength and Capacity Expansion The Company's balance sheet reflects a capital expenditure cycle nearing completion during FY26.
Balance sheet & cash: Dividend Based on the Company's performance, the Directors are pleased to recommend a Dividend of ₹ 9.00 per equity share, i.e.450 % of the face value of ₹2 each, for approval of the Members at the ensuing Annual General Meeting.

The Company's low leverage, with finance costs of just ` 1.8 crore for the full year and a largely debt free balance sheet, alongside an equity base of over ` 5,000 crore and current investments of about ` 1,875.3 crore, provides considerable financial headroom to fund further capacity additions without straining the capital structure.

SEBI/HO/DDHS/CIR/P/2018/144 dated November 26, 2018 mandated that the ‘Large Corporates' as defined under the said circular, shall raise not less than 25% of their incremental borrowings by way of issuance of debt securities, as defined under the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Debt Securities) Regulations, 2008.
Risks & challenges: According to the International Monetary Fund's latest assessments, global GDP growth is projected to moderate to around 3.3% in 2026, reflecting a slowdown from previous years but remaining stable under the assumption of contained geopolitical conflicts, particularly in the Middle East.
